Create a technology-appropriate ISNVFilter

Source: R/adaptive-filter.R
adaptiveFilter.Rd

Returns an ISNVFilter with default thresholds tuned for the error profile and read characteristics of the specified sequencing technology.

Usage

adaptiveFilter(technology = c("illumina", "ont", "pacbio_hifi", "generic"))

Arguments

technology

Character scalar. One of "illumina", "ont", "pacbio_hifi", or "generic".

Value

An ISNVFilter object.

Details

Each technology has distinct error modes that motivate different default thresholds:

Illumina (minFreq = 0.03, minDepth = 100)

Illumina short reads have low per-base error rates (~0.1–0.5%) but systematic context-dependent errors. A 3% frequency threshold safely exceeds the noise floor while retaining true low-frequency variants. Grubaugh et al. (2019) measured iSNVs above 3% accurately from at least 1,000 RNA copies sequenced to at least 400x, so 100x is a permissive floor; low-frequency false positives inflate diversity estimates markedly (McCrone & Lauring 2016).

Oxford Nanopore (ONT) (minFreq = 0.10, minDepth = 60, maxStrandBias = Inf)

ONT reads have higher per-base error rates (~1–5% with R10 chemistry), requiring a more conservative frequency threshold of 10% to avoid false positives; Bull et al. (2020) found that ONT sequencing does not accurately detect variants at low read-count frequencies, and reported over 99% sensitivity and precision for single-nucleotide variants above about 60-fold depth, which sets the depth threshold. Strand bias filtering is disabled (Inf) rather than given an untested threshold; supply maxStrandBias explicitly when the data support one.

PacBio HiFi (minFreq = 0.05, minDepth = 50)

HiFi consensus reads reach about 99.8% read accuracy via circular consensus sequencing (Wenger et al. 2019), allowing a frequency threshold below ONT but above Illumina. Depth of 50x reflects the lower throughput but high per-read accuracy.

Generic

Falls back to the standard ISNVFilter defaults (minFreq = 0.03, minDepth = 100), suitable for Illumina or when the technology is unknown.

References

McCrone JT, Lauring AS (2016). Measurements of intrahost viral diversity are extremely sensitive to systematic errors in variant calling. J Virol 90:6884-6895. doi:10.1128/JVI.00667-16

Grubaugh ND et al. (2019). An amplicon-based sequencing framework for accurately measuring intrahost virus diversity using PrimalSeq and iVar. Genome Biology 20:8. doi:10.1186/s13059-018-1618-7

Bull RA et al. (2020). Analytical validity of nanopore sequencing for rapid SARS-CoV-2 genome analysis. Nature Communications 11:6272. doi:10.1038/s41467-020-20075-6

Wenger AM et al. (2019). Accurate circular consensus long-read sequencing improves variant detection and assembly of a human genome. Nature Biotechnology 37:1155–1162. doi:10.1038/s41587-019-0217-9

See also

ISNVFilter for the underlying constructor, flagISNV for applying filters.

Examples

# Illumina defaults
adaptiveFilter("illumina")
#> ISNVFilter object
#>   minDepth:      100 
#>   freq range:   [0.03, 0.5]
#>   minAltReads:   10 
#>   maxStrandBias: 10 
#>   replicateConc: none

# ONT with strand bias disabled
filt <- adaptiveFilter("ont")
slot(filt, "maxStrandBias")  # Inf
#> [1] Inf

# PacBio HiFi
adaptiveFilter("pacbio_hifi")
#> ISNVFilter object
#>   minDepth:      50 
#>   freq range:   [0.05, 0.5]
#>   minAltReads:   10 
#>   maxStrandBias: 10 
#>   replicateConc: none

# Generic (same as ISNVFilter())
adaptiveFilter("generic")
#> ISNVFilter object
#>   minDepth:      100 
#>   freq range:   [0.03, 0.5]
#>   minAltReads:   10 
#>   maxStrandBias: 10 
#>   replicateConc: none
